structure: Part 3, listing and searching addresses (repo at HEAD 83fd1dd). Read in full: address/OperatorController.java (367 lines; claimed only the list handler, lines 70-132), address/OperatorService.java (222 lines; claimed list, queryPage and toPartialMatchRegex, lines 37-117), address/OperatorRepository.java (49 lines; claimed the three search queries and the status finder), address/OperatorPageResponse.java (45 lines), docs/openapi/operators.yml (491 lines; the GET /organisation/{orgId}/addresses operation and the OperatorPageResponse schema), docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml (441 lines; its description's Search and Pagination conventions and the list operation), README.md section API overview (lines 111-160; list row, list query parameters, wire conventions), and the tests OperatorListIT (9 tests), AddressSearchIT (10 tests), OperatorRepositoryIT (4 tests, 2 of them search) and OperatorServiceTest (list and search cases: 12 tests). Covered: the one list endpoint, its three query parameters (page, q, countryCode) with defaults, trimming and blank handling, its responses (200, 400 out-of-range or non-numeric page or missing header, 404, 500), the page size (server-configured, default 25, request parameters ignored), 1-based page numbering and the totals, every field of the page response, the search rules (fields matched, case-insensitive, partial, literal not regex, multi-word as one phrase), the OR combination of q and countryCode, the countryCode exact match, newest-first sort with an id tie-break, the ACTIVE-only and organisation-only listing, and the cv-025 and cv-048 rulings. The single-address operations, the address fields and validation, and the identity filter belong to other parts and are claimed only where the list operation depends on them.

claims.statement: The address book lists an organisation's addresses with GET /organisation/{orgId}/addresses.
The list operation requires the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header, and the path orgId must match it before any listing happens.
claims.note: How the header is enforced is part 4's; claimed here only as a precondition of the list.

claims.statement: A list request whose path orgId does not match the caller's organisation header returns 404 as a problem response.
claims.quote:
'404':
          description: Path orgId does not match the caller's organisation header

claims.statement: The list searches using the organisation id taken from the caller's header, so it only ever returns that organisation's addresses.
The list takes an optional page query parameter: a 1-based page number that defaults to 1.
claims.quote:
description = "1-based page number",
              schema = @Schema(type = "integer", format = "int32", minimum = "1", defaultValue = "1"))
          @RequestParam(defaultValue = "1")
          int page,

claims.statement: The list takes an optional q query parameter: a free-text search term.
The list takes an optional countryCode query parameter: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.
claims.quote: @param countryCode optional ISO alpha-2 country code (FE-resolved, cv-048)

claims.statement: Ruling cv-048: the countryCode filter value is resolved by the frontend, so the address book receives a country code rather than a country name.
claims.quote: cv-048: "optional ISO alpha-2 country code (FE-resolved, cv-048)"
claims.note: No ruling ledger file exists in the repo; this is the ruling's only wording, in Javadoc.

claims.statement: The list takes no page-size parameter: the page size is set on the server, defaulting to 25.
claims.ref: README.md: API overview, Wire conventions; docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml:20
claims.quote: Page size is server-configured (default **25** via `address-book.list.page-size`), not a request parameter.

claims.statement: Ruling cv-025: the page size is a server-side configuration, not a request parameter.
claims.quote:
cv-025: "The page size is a server-side config (cv-025),
   * not a request parameter."

claims.statement: The page size is read from the address-book.list.page-size setting and is 25 when that setting is absent; application.yml does not set it, so the running service uses 25.
claims.note: The absence from application.yml was checked with a grep for a list: key, which found none.

claims.statement: A page number below 1 is rejected as a bad request with the detail "page must be 1 or greater".
An out-of-range or non-numeric page returns 400 as a bad-request problem with no errors map.
claims.quote:
an out-of-range or non-numeric value is a 400
   * bad-request problem with no {@code errors} map.

claims.statement: The list's 400 response covers an out-of-range page, a non-numeric page, and a missing organisation header.
claims.quote:
'400':
          description: An out-of-range or non-numeric page, or a missing org header

claims.statement: An unexpected failure while listing returns 500 as a problem response.
Every list error response is served as application/problem+json.
A page number beyond the last page returns 200 with an empty items list, the requested page number and the real totals, not an error.
The list response is a top-level object with items and pagination metadata, never a bare array.
claims.quote:
List responses are a top-level object (`items`, `page`, `pageSize`, `totalItems`, `totalPages`),
  never a bare array.

claims.statement: The page response field items holds the addresses on this page, each in the single-address response shape, and is always present.
claims.quote:
description = "Addresses on this page",
            requiredMode = Schema.RequiredMode.REQUIRED)
        List<OperatorResponse> items,

claims.statement: The page response field page is the current 1-based page number, at least 1, and is always present.
claims.quote:
description = "Current 1-based page number",
            requiredMode = Schema.RequiredMode.REQUIRED,
            minimum = "1")
        int page,

claims.statement: The page response field pageSize is the server-configured page size, at least 1, and is always present.
claims.quote:
description = "Server-configured page size (cv-025)",
            requiredMode = Schema.RequiredMode.REQUIRED,
            minimum = "1")
        int pageSize,

claims.statement: The page response field totalItems is the total number of matching addresses across all pages, at least 0, and is always present.
claims.quote:
description = "Total number of matching addresses",
            requiredMode = Schema.RequiredMode.REQUIRED,
            minimum = "0")
        int totalItems,

claims.statement: The page response field totalPages is the total number of pages, at least 0, and is always present.
claims.quote:
description = "Total number of pages",
            requiredMode = Schema.RequiredMode.REQUIRED,
            minimum = "0")
        int totalPages)

claims.statement: The page response echoes the page number the caller asked for, not one derived from the result.
claims.quote:
return new OperatorPageResponse(
          items, page, pageSize, (int) result.getTotalElements(), result.getTotalPages());

claims.statement: The page response fields are camelCase on the wire.
The list returns only ACTIVE addresses: soft-deleted addresses (tombstones) never appear in it.
claims.quote:
One page of the organisation's ACTIVE addresses, newest first. Scoped to {@code organisationId};
   * DELETED tombstones are excluded because the query pins {@code status ACTIVE}.

claims.statement: Every list path, plain, q, countryCode or both, is pinned to the ACTIVE status and the caller's organisation.
The list is sorted newest first by creation time.
claims.quote: | `GET` | `/organisation/{orgId}/addresses` | Paginated list of ACTIVE addresses (newest first) |

claims.statement: Addresses created at the same moment are ordered by id, descending, so the order is stable from page to page.
claims.note: That this makes paging stable is inferred from the tie-break; the code states only the sort.

claims.statement: Search results use the same newest-first order as the plain list; the caller cannot choose a sort order.
claims.quote:
Pageable pageable =
        PageRequest.of(
            page - 1,
            pageSize,
            Sort.by(Sort.Direction.DESC, "createdAt")...
claims.note: One pageable is built before the search path is chosen, and the endpoint has no sort parameter.

claims.statement: The list read is served by the org_status_created index.
claims.quote:
the sort is {@code createdAt} descending, served by the
   * {@code org_status_created} index.
claims.note: The index itself is part 1's (Address entity, README Indexes).

claims.statement: The q search matches the address's name, town or city, and postcode, and no other field.
The q search does not match address line 1, address line 2, county, phone or email.
claims.note: Follows from the three fields the query names; AddressSearchIT proves it for addressLine1 only.

claims.statement: The q search is case-insensitive.
The q search is a partial match: the term can appear anywhere in a field, including inside a word.
The q term is matched literally: characters with special meaning in a pattern are treated as plain text.
A q term of several words is matched as one phrase, not as separate words.
claims.note: The whole trimmed term is quoted as one literal; the test only proves a contiguous phrase matches, not that out-of-order words fail.

claims.statement: Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed from q before searching.
A blank or whitespace-only q is ignored, and the list is returned unfiltered by text.
The countryCode filter matches the stored country code exactly.
The countryCode filter is case-sensitive: a lower-case code does not match an upper-case stored code.
claims.note: An equality match with no case option; country codes are stored as given (cv-011, part 1). No test covers a lower-case filter.

claims.statement: Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed from countryCode before filtering.
A blank or whitespace-only countryCode is ignored, and the list is returned unfiltered by country.
When q and countryCode are both given they combine with OR: an address is listed if the term matches its name, town or city, or postcode, or if its country code equals the filter.
claims.ref: README.md: List query parameters; docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml:18; OperatorRepository.java:37-42
claims.quote: | `countryCode` | When combined with `q`, matches addresses where **either** the search term appears in `name`/`townOrCity`/`postcode` **or** the stored `countryCode` equals this value (OR semantics, not AND) |

claims.statement: The locked contract fixes OR semantics for q with countryCode.
claims.quote: **Search:** `q` and `countryCode` combine with OR semantics when both are supplied.
claims.note: Because of the OR, adding a countryCode to a text search widens the results rather than narrowing them. Recorded, not reconciled.

claims.statement: There is no filter on address type or usage in the list: the only filters are q and countryCode.
claims.note: Consistent with cv-044 (the address book is untyped and unroled), which another part claims.

claims.statement: The list totals and page count reflect the search: totalItems counts only the matching addresses.
claims.quote: Page<Address> result = queryPage(organisationId, q, countryCode, pageable);

claims.statement: The list request is logged with the page, whether a search term was given (not the term itself), and the country code.
claims.quote: log.info("GET addresses - page {}, q present {}, countryCode {}", page, q != null, countryCode);

claims.statement: The list endpoint and its database query are each timed as metrics.
The locked contract does not state a minimum for page, while the generated contract states minimum 1.
claims.quote:
- name: page
        in: query
        required: false
        schema:
          type: integer
          format: int32
          default: 1
claims.note: Both contracts agree on the default; the server rejects page below 1 either way.

claims.statement: Tested: with 30 addresses, page 1 returns 25 items, page 1, pageSize 25, totalItems 30, totalPages 2, and the newest address first.
Tested: page 2 of 30 addresses returns the remaining 5, none of which appeared on page 1.
Tested: soft-deleted addresses are left out of the list and its totals, and every listed item has deleted false.
Tested: another organisation's addresses never appear in the caller's list.
Tested: page 0 or -1 returns 400 with problem type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/bad-request, title "Bad Request" and no errors map.
Tested: page_size and pageSize request parameters are ignored, and the server's 25 applies.
Tested: a non-numeric page such as abc returns 400 as a bad-request problem with no errors map.
Tested: a list request with no organisation header returns 400 as a bad-request problem with no errors map.
Tested: a partial, lower-case term (gree) matches a name (Green Farm), and does not match an address whose only match is in address line 1.
Tested: a partial term (inver) matches the town or city (Inverness).
Tested: a multi-word term (green valley) and an upper-case term (GREEN) both match the name Green Valley Livestock Farm.
Tested: a partial lower-case term (iv2) matches the postcode IV2 3JH.
Tested: the term .* is treated as literal text and matches nothing.
Tested: countryCode FR returns only the caller's addresses stored with FR, not GB ones and not another organisation's FR ones.
Tested: the countryCode filter leaves out soft-deleted addresses.
Tested: q France with countryCode FR returns both an FR address that does not contain the text and a GB address whose name contains France.
Tested: a q search leaves out soft-deleted addresses and other organisations' addresses.
Tested: 30 search matches paginate as 25 then 5, and the two pages together hold every match exactly once.
Tested at the database: the countryCode query is organisation-scoped and leaves out deleted addresses.
Tested at the database: the combined q and countryCode query is organisation-scoped.
Unit-tested: the service turns the 1-based page into the database's 0-based page, uses the configured size, and sorts by createdAt descending.
Unit-tested: a configured page size (10) is used in the query and reported as pageSize.
Unit-tested: the service builds a 25-item first page and a 5-item second page from 30 matches, with totalPages 2, and rejects page 0 as a bad request.
Unit-tested: q alone uses the text search, countryCode alone uses the country filter, both use the combined search, and padded values are trimmed first.
claims.quote:
service.list(ORG, 1, "  farm  ", null);

    // Then — trim is applied before regex construction

claims.statement: Unit-tested: a whitespace-only q or countryCode falls back to the unfiltered list.
No test proves the list's 404 for a path orgId that does not match the header; the list tests cover only a missing header.
claims.note: Looked in OperatorListIT, AddressSearchIT and the list cases of OperatorServiceTest. A mismatch test may live in part 4's identity tests.

claims.statement: No test proves that the countryCode filter is case-sensitive, nor what a lower-case code returns.
No test proves that the q search does not match county, address line 2, phone or email; only address line 1 is proven excluded.
The list sets no upper limit on the length of q or countryCode.
claims.note: Neither the handler nor either contract gives a maxLength or validation for these two parameters.
